headline: High: Devin can read/write shared workspaces and external services while dbt-core can touch warehouse data, creating default-path leakage, conflict, and compliance risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browsers, and shared integrations, so it may ingest dbt-core outputs from files or tickets; dbt-core can emit warehouse-derived artifacts. No direct shared channel is documented, but the interaction is plausible through workspace files or Slack/GitHub handoffs, so uncertainty stays above low.
conditions: IF Devin is given dbt-generated files or tickets as instructions, prompt-like content can steer its actions.
IF dbt-core outputs are copied into a shared workspace or integration channel, Devin may parse them as authoritative.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of dbt artifacts into Devin prompts.
Require a human review step before Devin acts on dbt outputs.
Separate instruction channels from data artifacts in shared integrations.
Use provenance labels on files and tickets.
requires-engineering: add content-type filtering for agent-to-agent handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted egress, while Devin reads filesystem contents, repo clones, and writes to GitHub/Slack/Jira/Notion. Even without a shared filesystem explicitly stated, the pair can move sensitive warehouse-derived data into Devin-managed integrations in default workflows.
conditions: IF dbt artifacts contain warehouse data and are placed in Devin-accessible files or tickets, leakage becomes possible.
IF Devin is connected to GitHub, Slack, Jira, or Notion with sensitive content, that content can leave the original workspace.
mitigations: Restrict Devin to redacted dbt outputs only.
Block sensitive warehouse tables from being materialized into shared artifacts.
Review outbound Slack/Jira/Notion writes before enabling them.
Use separate service accounts for dbt and Devin.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on shared integrations.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and parallel sessions with shared integrations; dbt-core can call warehouse APIs and egress. If both operate on the same repo or project, concurrent edits and git state changes can collide in default workflows, and the blast radius includes irreversible repo history or broken deployments.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or workspace, concurrent writes can race.
IF Devin and dbt-core both modify project files or generated artifacts, git conflicts can occur without locking.
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent.
Pause Devin while dbt runs on the same repo.
Require lockfiles or lease tokens for shared workspaces.
Review and merge changes manually.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can autonomously act inside its workspace and write to external systems, while dbt-core can produce warehouse-facing outputs. If Devin treats dbt outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits, tickets, or Slack updates; the pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced as a default behavior.
conditions: IF Devin uses dbt-generated artifacts as ground truth without verification, downstream actions can propagate mistakes.
IF dbt-core emits incorrect model metadata and Devin commits or reports it, the error spreads to other systems.
mitigations: Require validation before Devin acts on dbt outputs.
Add checksum or schema checks on generated artifacts.
Limit Devin's write access to non-production channels.
Have a human approve commits and tickets.
requires-engineering: implement automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, and Devin handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs with broad cloud egress and write scopes. If warehouse data includes regulated or residency-bound content, routing it through Devin-managed integrations can create retention and jurisdiction mismatches; the profiles do not prove a specific regime, so uncertainty is escalated only to medium.
conditions: IF warehouse data includes regulated personal data and is copied into Devin integrations, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention or deletion requests must cover both dbt artifacts and Devin-managed tickets, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Devin-managed channels.
Use separate retention policies for analytics artifacts and tickets.
Document data residency for each integration.
Review access scopes before enabling writes.
requires-engineering: align DPA and retention controls across systems.
